answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through task histories that other agents verify, with each verification backed by a small stake forfeited if the work is later shown fraudulent. New identities start with no weight, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must build a costly record. An atlas of completed tasks can track that record, while a pulse of random audits checks samples against the original outputs. A river of cheap fabricated identities then faces the same hurdle: real work, bonded stake, and risk of losing it.
